report:
ELVIA Scientific Verification Report
I25-40136 / 0032
Paper: Position: Supervised Classifiers Answer the Wrong Questions for OOD Detection
Inspection outcome: Major: two invalid core inferences (universal irreducible-error floor and unrestricted posterior collapse); one bounded Minor release concern
Reviewed version: ICML 2025, PMLR 267:81689-81713; frozen 25-page publisher-linked PDF
Batch token: `[internal identifier omitted]`
Review date: 24 October 2026 (America/Chicago); machine logs use UTC
# 1. Identity, inspection scope and decisive result

Authors: Yucen Lily Li, Daohan Lu, Polina Kirichenko, Shikai Qiu, Tim G. J. Rudner, C. Bayan Bruss and Andrew Gordon Wilson. The original source [S1], papers/0032/0032.pdf, has 25 pages and 13,167,636 bytes. SHA-256: c5538524c261f5e3a7f1c3e8c10d8c81a4f2d6a1929a9ae36d3b29a7d467e1e2. The hash matches its controller receipt; title, authors and imprint agree with the publisher record. Page references mean one-based PDF/printed local pages, not global proceedings pagination.

Main Sections 1-6, Appendix A.1-A.7 and the implementation descriptions in Appendix B were inspected. The public repository was preserved at commit 124502380ffa4ac70731fd305a026044f8e005f9 and read statically. Independent checks cover an exact AUROC counterexample, a Bayesian nonidentification example, the Gaussian density toy example and aggregation of the printed Table A.1.

The Major finding is specific: a trained linear ID/OOD oracle cannot certify the best performance of every feature-based detector. Therefore its residual does not identify the paper’s claimed irreducible component or establish the method-independent error floor used in Sections 4.1 and 5.6. This does not show that the reported ImageNet scores are numerically wrong or that supervised features never have genuine limitations. A second Major finding concerns the unrestricted posterior-collapse derivation used in the core epistemic-uncertainty argument and method guidance. The released command-line evaluation path is a separate Minor concern. Figure 7’s class configuration remains unresolved.
# 2. Definitions and review assumptions

Let h be a fixed feature representation, P the ID feature distribution, Q the OOD feature distribution, and s(h) an OOD score, with larger values indicating OOD. For independent H_P~P and H_Q~Q, AUROC(s)=Pr[s(H_Q)>s(H_P)]+0.5 Pr[s(H_Q)=s(H_P)]. This is a pairwise ranking measure, not directly a fraction of individually unclassifiable images.

A binary linear classifier followed by a two-class softmax produces a score monotone in one affine function of h. It is a restricted member of the set of all feature-based scores. Training it on ID and OOD data gives it privileged labels, but does not remove its function-class restriction. The counterexample below permits infinite training data and exact optimization; it is not an optimization-failure complaint.

The Bayesian check uses the paper’s general stochastic-parameter formulation and a proper prior. The code findings concern the preserved public snapshot and documented commands; the code that actually generated published figures has not been established. Author code was not executed.
# 3. Problem 1: a linear oracle does not establish irreducible feature error

Source claim and location. Section 4.1, p. 4, first describes an oracle as a binary linear classifier trained to distinguish ID and OOD features, then treats 1 minus its AUROC as irreducible error that no feature-based method can reduce. Figure 2, p. 5, uses that interpretation in its error decomposition. Section 5.6, p. 9, uses the same argument for a greater-than-5% irreducible residual in the large DINOv2 representation. The released implementation explicitly constructs torch.nn.Linear(feature_dim,2), ood_score.py line 92 [S1-S3, E1-E3].

Suspect step. Let A_all be the supremum of AUROC over all permitted feature-based scores, and A_lin the best affine-score AUROC. Set inclusion gives the inequality below. An observed finite-trained oracle is no better a universal ceiling. The direction needed for the paper’s universal residual floor is not justified.

\[A_{\mathrm{all}}\ge A_{\mathrm{lin}},\qquad 1-A_{\mathrm{all}}\le 1-A_{\mathrm{lin}}.\] Complete counterexample. Set h(x)=x in one dimension. ID features take -1 and +1 with equal probability; OOD features take -2 and +2 with equal probability. The two ID classes are their signs, so a supervised linear classifier using this same representation classifies the ID labels perfectly. All four support points are distinct; no overlap or feature ambiguity is present. No assumption in the oracle argument requires continuous features or excludes these distributions.

For s(h)=w h+b with w>0, the OOD point +2 beats both ID points and -2 beats neither: two wins among four equally likely pairs, so AUROC=1/2. For w<0 the ordering reverses and again gives two wins. For w=0 every pair ties and AUROC=1/2. The two-class linear-softmax oracle has the same ordering. Yet s(h)=|h| or h^2 ranks both OOD points above both ID points, giving AUROC=1. This proves the claim for every affine score, rather than only for the finite coefficients checked by the independent script.
Quantity | Linear oracle | Nonlinear score using identical features
ID scores (example) | -1, +1 | 1, 1 using h^2
OOD scores (example) | -2, +2 | 4, 4 using h^2
AUROC | 1/2 for every affine score | 1
Residual 1-AUROC | 1/2 | 0

Alternative reading and counterevidence. The word ’proxy’ would support use of the oracle as an empirical comparator. It cannot support the subsequent assertion that no feature-based detector can do better. Exact equality of ID and OOD feature laws would indeed imply indistinguishability; the counterexample does not dispute that statement. It shows that failure of a linear discriminator does not establish such equality. Nor does it establish zero Bayes error for the actual ImageNet-derived feature distributions.

Supported impact and judgment. Major, limited to a substantial invalid inference underlying the central quantitative irreducible-error decomposition and universal floor. The reported comparisons among the named baselines remain empirical observations. The general warning that ID classification objectives need not guarantee OOD detection is not refuted.

Precise repair. Rename the quantity a linear-oracle residual and remove its interpretation as a universal irreducible component. The gap to the best tested score can still be reported descriptively. Richer held-out probes can test whether additional feature information is usable, but even a failed nonlinear probe is not by itself a proof of a Bayes upper bound. Establishing the actual irreducible error requires justified distributional assumptions or a valid bound. The revised interpretation is logically verified; the real-data residual cannot be repaired numerically without fresh analysis.
# 4. Problem 2: unrestricted posterior collapse need not occur

Source claim and location. Section 5.3, p. 7, states that in the infinite-ID-data limit the posterior over model parameters collapses, and uses this to argue that epistemic uncertainty cannot retain an OOD signal. Section 6, p. 9, extends the decreasing-usefulness interpretation. This statement needs identification conditions on parameters that affect the OOD inputs. It is not a consequence of increasing ID sample size alone [S1, E1].

Assumption-satisfying example. Consider a two-class logistic network p(Y=1|x,theta)=sigmoid(theta1*x1+theta2*x2), with independent proper priors theta_j in {-log 3,+log 3}, each equally likely. ID inputs are (1,0) and (-1,0), with labels generated by the specified model. The likelihood of any ID dataset is independent of theta2, so its posterior remains exactly its prior at every sample size, even if theta1 is learned perfectly. At the OOD input x=(0,1), the two possible predictive probabilities remain 1/4 and 3/4.

\[p(Y=1\mid x=(0,1),D)=\frac12,\qquad I(Y;\theta\mid x=(0,1),D)=1-h_2(1/4)=0.1887218755\ \mathrm{bits}.\] Here h2 is binary entropy in bits. The positive mutual information persists for every finite n and in the infinite-data limit because the ID likelihood contains no theta2 term. The independent checker evaluates the exact posterior symmetry and entropy, and the reasoning establishes the all-n statement.

Continuous proper-prior check. The same failure occurs with independent theta1 and theta2 uniformly distributed on [-log 3, log 3], so it does not rely on a discrete interpretation of the parameter integral. ID inputs (1,0) and (-1,0), each with positive probability, have model-generated labels. For every ID dataset, the likelihood contains only theta1; posterior(theta2|D) therefore equals its proper uniform prior exactly. At x=(0,1), symmetry gives predictive probability 1/2, while epistemic mutual information is 1 minus the prior expectation of h2(sigmoid(theta2)). Half the prior mass has |theta2| at least log(3)/2, providing the positive bound below.

\[I(Y;\theta\mid (0,1),D)\geq \frac{1-h_2(\sqrt{3}/(1+\sqrt{3}))}{2}>0,\] The bound is approximately 0.0262143336 bits and is independent of ID sample size. Strict positivity is analytic: binary entropy is strictly less than one away from probability 1/2. This establishes failure of unrestricted collapse, not any real-data AUROC or guaranteed detection success. The controller proof and independent arithmetic are retained in verification/0032/revisions/severity_calibration_controller_001/evidence/.

Alternative interpretation and impact. For an identifiable finite-parameter model with posterior consistency and continuous predictions at the query point, posterior concentration can make predictive epistemic uncertainty vanish. That restricted rationale is defensible. It does not yield a general monotonic AUROC claim, and it does not apply when ID observations leave OOD-relevant directions unidentified. The displayed finite last-layer Laplace experiment is not refuted by this example.

Judgment: Major for the invalid unrestricted derivation. Section 5.3 uses posterior collapse to explain a fundamental mismatch with OOD detection; Section 6 carries that argument into its data-size deterioration claim and guidance on Bayesian/ensemble methods when ID data are abundant. This is a direct dependency of a core technical argument, not an isolated observation. Survival of the finite Laplace scores or the broad position does not downgrade this separate error. Repair: state identification and posterior-concentration conditions for every OOD-relevant parameter direction, retain the finite experiment within its actual scope, and withdraw the unconditional data-size inference. A conditional concentration statement alone also does not prove a universal monotone AUROC trend. No universally reliable epistemic OOD detector is claimed.
# 5. Problem 3: released CLI and oracle routing are inconsistent

Source claim and location. Appendix B, p. 25, links the public reproduction repository. Its README provides python extract_features.py and python ood_score.py commands. Static inspection of the preserved commit identifies multiple linked blockers in that documented workflow [S3, E3].
Location | Observed source | Static consequence
ood_score.py:204 | if __name__ == ’main’: | Normal direct invocation sets __name__ to ’__main__’; the parser/evaluation block is not entered, assuming imports succeed.

ood_score.py:205-206,232,248 | linear_oracle belongs to both logit_methods and feature_methods; if/elif dispatch checks logits first | After correcting the guard, linear_oracle is captured by the logit branch, which has no corresponding oracle call.
ood_score.py:87,97,264 | Fourth formal parameter is ood_train_features; caller passes train_labels | The intended oracle-training OOD feature matrix is not supplied; labels are used in its place.

extract_features.py:266; get_dataset.py:95 | get_dataset(dataset_name) omits required dataset_dir | The documented extraction call does not pass the directory required by the preserved helper signature.

Complete check. Source was parsed with Python’s AST machinery without importing or executing author modules. The guard is a comparison of distinct string values under standard direct invocation. Dispatch membership and if/elif control flow establish the unreachable oracle branch. The call’s positional arguments were matched to its declared signature; the dataset helper likewise has a required directory parameter. The complete files and exact lines are retained, so these checks do not depend on a summarized code fragment.

Counterevidence and scope. Functions may have been invoked manually from unshared notebooks or a different historical tree. The defects establish a problem in the released documented workflow; they do not establish which code generated the paper’s numerical results. No runtime failure is falsely reported as observed: this was static inspection only.

Judgment: Minor for released reproducibility. A local guard correction to ’__main__’ repairs that control-flow condition, and passing the parsed dataset directory repairs that missing positional argument. Full oracle repair also requires unambiguous dispatch and a separate OOD training-feature input distinct from held-out evaluation data. These are supported repair requirements, not a tested end-to-end patch. No author files were modified and no full repair has been validated.
# 6. Needs Evidence: Figure 7 class configuration

Section 5.4, p. 8, describes ID={keyboard, porcupine} and training OOD={cup, skyscraper}. The title inside Figure 7 instead gives ID={shrew, porcupine} and OOD={cup, bowl}. The original PDF page was rendered and both passages visually confirmed. These configurations change the semantic relationships used in the BERT-similarity argument.

The public repository does not supply the unseen-class training/BERT-similarity experiment or run metadata that resolves the discrepancy. A mislabeled plot or stale prose is a plausible explanation, but the evidence does not determine which one. The unresolved item is the identity of this experiment and its relation to the plotted values, not proof that those values are wrong. Judgment: Needs Evidence. Obtain the class-selection/run record before selecting a correction; no replacement configuration is invented.
# 7. Checks that passed and dependencies of the conclusions

Table A.1, p. 18: independent arithmetic over all 42 printed rows gives mean FPR@95 values of 66.5214% (MSP), 61.5476% (max logit), 62.6095% (entropy) and 61.9024% (energy). The rounded MSP mean of 66.5% and the statement that each average exceeds 60% are supported. This recomputes equal-setting-weighted printed-number means, not thresholds or predictions.

Appendix A.6 Gaussian toy: for ID N(0,1), OOD N(2,1), and density model N(mu,1), the reviewer derivation gives AUROC=a*b+(1-a)*(1-b), with a=Phi(sqrt(2)) and b=Phi(sqrt(2)*(1-mu)). It gives 0.8550723132 at mu=0 and approaches 0.9213503965 as mu tends to negative infinity, while KL from the ID distribution grows as mu^2/2. The limiting tradeoff described in the paper is consistent; the ’optimum at negative infinity’ is a supremum rather than a finite fitted mean.

The oracle PCA uses ID and OOD features by explicit design and searches a stated component-count set. It is a disclosed hindsight comparator, not hidden leakage. Its performance likewise does not certify a globally optimal feature detector. Appendix B.1 reports three-seed averages for the outlier-exposure comparison; no missing-seed allegation is made. The observed harm in selected settings can support a ’can hurt’ claim.

Scaling comparisons mix architecture, objective and pretraining data. They support descriptive comparisons among tested models, rather than an isolated causal scaling law. Appendix A.5 discusses pretraining exposure to related data. These limits do not negate the observed scores; the unsupported universal irreducibility interpretation is already covered by Problem 1.

Problem 1 is independent of Problems 2 and 3 and of the Figure 7 mismatch. Repairing the public script cannot turn a linear oracle into a Bayes performance bound. The paper’s distinction between label uncertainty and distribution membership remains useful within the inspected scope.
# 8. Versions, conclusion table and remaining work

The separate arXiv version is Out-of-Distribution Detection Methods Answer the Wrong Questions, arXiv:2507.01831v1, submitted 2 July 2025 and labeled an extended ICML version by its authors. Targeted comparison retains the linear-oracle irreducibility statements, unrestricted posterior-collapse rationale and Figure 7 class mismatch. It is preserved separately and does not replace the exact publisher-linked source. The examined arXiv history lists v1 only; no explicit correction was identified in the scoped source search.

No trained models, datasets or published prediction arrays were rerun. Human scientific decisions and author adoption remain pending. More expressive held-out feature probes, an appropriate theoretical bound, resolved experiment configuration and corrected reproducible code would address different parts of the remaining work.

ELVIA Scientific Verification Report
I25-40137 / 0033
Paper: Position: AI Scaling: From Up to Down and Out
Inspection outcome: Minor: federated-learning privacy guarantee exceeds what raw-data locality establishes
Reviewed version: ICML 2025, PMLR 267:82252-82264; frozen 13-page publisher-linked PDF
Batch token: `[internal identifier omitted]`
Review date: Review and severity calibration: 24 October 2026 (America/Chicago); machine logs use UTC
# 1. Identity, checked scope and outcome

Authors: Yunke Wang, Yanxi Li and Chang Xu. The reviewed source [S1] is papers/0033/0033.pdf, 13 pages and 238,510 bytes. Its SHA-256 is `809c026bcc8c16ee6691ed5e2504f01cf0a1440822432677a446261201b70548`, matching the controller acquisition receipt. Title, author line and proceedings record agree. Locations below use one-based PDF/printed local pages, not global proceedings page numbers.

The review covered the substantive Sections 1-8, pp. 1-9, the Impact Statement on p. 10, the distinction among model size, active compute and training state, and the logical status of the proposed applications. This is a position paper proposing a research roadmap, not a paper establishing a formal scaling theorem or reporting a new comparative experiment.

One bounded technical-foundation claim is false as stated: sharing gradients or model updates while retaining raw data locally does not ensure privacy and security. The report gives an exact independent reconstruction example and attributes the broader known limitation to prior gradient-leakage research [S3]. No new attack or failure of the overall Up/Down/Out framework is claimed.
# 2. Problem 1: local data storage does not guarantee private updates

Source claim and exact location. Section 4.2, p. 7, states that federated learning ensures data privacy and security because raw data stay local and only model updates, such as gradients, are shared. The healthcare example then infers compliance with privacy regulations from training without sharing raw patient data. No secure-aggregation protocol, formal privacy guarantee, update-observation restriction or noise mechanism is specified for this claim [S1].

Suspect inference. Raw-data locality is a statement about where records are stored and directly transmitted. Confidentiality is a statement about what another party can learn from the released messages. A gradient can encode the record even though the record itself is never transmitted. The premise therefore does not entail the stated guarantee.

Definitions and assumptions. Consider a client training a linear predictor f(x)=w^T x+b on one record (x,y), using squared loss L=0.5(f(x)-y)^2. Let the coordinating server observe the client gradient with respect to both w and b. This is an ordinary gradient-sharing instance of the broad setting described in the paper; the source imposes no minimum local batch size and no mechanism concealing individual updates. The raw record remains on the client.

\[r=w^\top x+b-y,\qquad g_w=rx,\qquad g_b=r,\qquad x=\frac{g_w}{g_b}\ \ (g_b\ne0).\] Complete finite example. Take x=(2,3), y=1, w=(0,0) and b=0. Then r=-1, so the shared messages are g_w=(-2,-3) and g_b=-1. Dividing the vector by the scalar recovers x=(2,3) exactly. The original claim’s premises hold: data are local, only a model gradient is shared, and the learning computation is valid. Nevertheless, the server learns the complete input. If the client instead transmits a one-step SGD model update with a common nonzero learning rate, the ratio of the weight and bias updates yields the same x.

The derivative identities prove the general one-record result whenever r is nonzero; the finite computation checks the stated parameters. This reviewer-owned calculation is not an execution of author code or a reproduction of the attack algorithm in [S3]. The source claim supplies no privacy metric or threat model under which the revealed input could still be regarded as protected.

Alternative readings and counterevidence. FL can reduce direct centralized collection of raw records, and a properly protected protocol can offer specific privacy properties. Neither point rescues a guarantee based solely on localization. Section 6, p. 9, calls for attention to privacy and security, and the p. 10 Impact Statement recognizes risks, but neither introduces a protection mechanism that excludes this example. The example does not claim that every FL system leaks every record, or that a specific hospital deployment uses this vulnerable configuration.

Calibrated judgment: Minor retained. The error removes the automatic privacy/security assurance and the resulting healthcare compliance inference. Its bounded role follows from the actual dependency structure: Section4.1, p.6, defines Scaling Out through specialized variants and connecting interfaces; Section4.2 offers FL alongside parameter-efficient adaptation, conditional control and coordination protocols. Neither specialization nor interoperation is derived from the false confidentiality premise. The error is an application-enabling assurance on one route, rather than a derivation or necessary generalization establishing the scaling axes. The saved example satisfies the stated data-locality and update-sharing conditions; later privacy cautions do not exclude it. Collaboration without centralizing raw records survives as an architectural capability, not a guarantee about released messages. This remains a known-issue reproduction attributed to Zhu, Liu and Han [S3].

Precise correction. Federated learning can avoid centralizing raw data, but confidentiality and security depend on the adversary model, which updates are visible, and the protections applied to those updates. Regulatory compliance cannot be concluded from FL alone. This wording removes the invalid implication while retaining the supported architectural benefit. No particular privacy mechanism or complete secure protocol is proposed as a verified repair; that would require a specified threat model and independent evaluation.
# 3. Other checked reasoning and interpretation limits

The Up/Down/Out framework organizes a research agenda. Section 7 explicitly acknowledges the continued value of scaling up and recommends balanced investment. It should not be read as a proof that all successful AI development must follow a mandatory sequence, or that scaling up can no longer yield gains.

Section 3.5 describes minimal functional modules as future work, not as an established theorem that all capabilities can be losslessly compressed. LoRA’s reduction in trainable adaptation state is distinct from reducing the full base-model parameter count. Sparse MoE active-parameter counts are likewise distinct from total stored parameters. The report preserves these resource distinctions without treating the roadmap’s discussion as a new complexity proof.

The blockchain paragraph in Section 4.3 is a future proposal without a concrete enforcement protocol. A ledger can support provenance but does not by itself specify how off-ledger actions are prevented. Manufacturing resilience, creative collaboration and ecosystem-wide energy savings are prospective scenarios. No newly implemented system or measured effect size is supplied for those scenarios, so this review does not fabricate a numerical failure or certify their realization.

The conclusion itself proposes evaluating FLOPs, latency, energy, cost-per-inference and performance-per-watt. Actual end-to-end savings depend on communication, aggregation, hardware, quality targets, reuse and total deployment volume. Such measurements would be needed to establish a specific efficiency or sustainability advantage. A need for future validation is recorded as scope, not automatically elevated to an error finding.

Quantitative hardware/model examples were spot-checked as context. Source-attribution ambiguities and isolated background numerical details were not used to infer a second substantive algorithmic or mathematical defect. This is not a comprehensive audit of every cited model specification or historical citation.
# 4. Versions, source availability and remaining work

The current author manuscript record lists arXiv:2502.01677v2, revised 13 May 2025, following v1 on 2 February 2025. Its separate 13-page PDF was preserved, and the targeted FL claim compared. The same unconditional privacy/security wording remains in v2. It is an alternative version; it does not replace the frozen PMLR source [S2].

No dedicated experiment repository or separate supplement was located in the inspected publisher/arXiv/author records. The Google A2A link is a referenced external protocol, not evidence of an implementation for this paper. OpenReview presented a browser-verification challenge, so its discussions and possible attachments were not fully reviewed. No explicit erratum was located in the scoped search; this does not establish global absence.

Sunayana Rane, ICML 2025 position paper [S1]. Page numbers below are the paper’s printed local pages 1-10, which equal one-based PDF pages; they are not the PMLR volume pagination. The frozen original is papers/0034/0034.pdf. Its 156,215 bytes and SHA-256 match the controller receipt. No original bytes were changed.

One Minor finding is retained after claim-level calibration. The Loomis account omits substantive limits and overstates the absence of information. Correcting it changes the extent of the claimed procedural deficit in that case. The corrected record still leaves the internal scoring weights undisclosed, which is the specific access limitation relevant to the explanation-to-contestation argument; the report does not infer adequacy or inadequacy of the real safeguards from that fact alone.

The inspection covered the abstract and Sections 1-7, both principal case studies, the interpretation discussion, alternative views, and selected primary references. It used source comparison and logical analysis, not empirical reproduction. There are no theorem proofs, benchmark tables, or released experimental results in this paper to reproduce. A broad policy position was not relabeled a mathematical impossibility theorem.
# 2. Definitions and limits that matter

Four objects must be kept separate: an algorithm’s input-to-score mapping; the reasons an official gives for an adverse decision; the recipient’s practical ability to correct or contest that decision; and the legal adequacy of the entire procedure. A model’s lack of complete mechanistic or causal explanation does not by itself specify all of the other three. Conversely, knowing a model’s coefficients does not by itself establish a fair or legally adequate procedure.

The paper itself limits constitutional due process to relevant government action (p. 1) and extends it to private activity as an ideal in Section 6 (p. 8). This distinction is retained. Mathews v. Eldridge, 424 U.S. 319, 334-335 [S4], evaluates procedural sufficiency in context using the private interest, risk of erroneous deprivation and value of extra safeguards, and government interests and burdens. K.W. applies that framework. Neither source supplies a universal requirement that every internal computation be understood. This is a scope clarification, not a claim that a particular opaque deployment is lawful.

The audit checks what the cited historical decisions say. It does not adjudicate a live case, establish the current law in every jurisdiction, or certify any AI system. Model code, individual case records, raw COMPAS data, and the underlying Idaho training records were not obtained or executed. No new estimate of bias, recidivism prediction, or benefit adequacy is claimed.
# 3. Problem 1: the Loomis account loses material conditions

Source claim and location. Case study 2, p. 6 right column, describes the permission to use COMPAS in sentencing largely through the existence of other reasons for the decision. After reproducing five cautions, p. 7 right column says the court has full discretion whether and how to take the list into account. Section 5, p. 8, summarizes the opposing position as permitting biased systems with a warning label. On p. 7 left column, the accompanying trade-secret discussion says courts have no information about the system whatsoever. These passages together imply a materially weaker set of safeguards and a more complete information vacuum than the primary opinion describes.

Decisive check. The official State v. Loomis opinion, 2016 WI 68, filed July 13, 2016 [S2], paragraph 98 says risk scores may not determine incarceration or sentence severity, and may not be the determinative factor in deciding whether an offender can be safely and effectively supervised in the community. Paragraph 99 requires the court to explain independent factors supporting the sentence. Paragraph 100 requires the written advisement and then separately lists the cautions. Thus, independent sentencing reasons and warning labels are not the entire rule. The prohibitions are express conditions of the permission described in paragraphs 8 and 120.

The information claim is also too absolute. Paragraphs 51-56 distinguish unavailable factor weights and risk-calculation details from information that is available: the defendant’s report, underlying questions and answers, criminal-history inputs, and portions of the practitioner’s guide. The majority reasons that the defendant can challenge relevant underlying information. Whether this is enough is open to the paper’s criticism, but it is not an absence of all information.

Alternative reading and counterevidence. Paragraph 71 gives sentencing courts discretion in assessing a risk tool’s accuracy, and the decision does not prescribe a numerical weight for each caution. The paper can reasonably question whether judges actually avoid cognitive bias or whether the safeguards work. Justice Abrahamson’s concurrence, paragraphs 132-135, expressly records the court’s limited understanding of COMPAS and calls for stronger on-record reasoning; this supports the paper’s concern. These points do not erase the majority’s substantive restrictions or convert partial disclosure into no disclosure. The review therefore does not assert that the court eliminated all discretion, that the warnings are empirically effective, or that the author’s normative disagreement is erroneous.

Bounded consequence and verified correction. Replace the blanket account with this statement: Loomis permitted consideration of COMPAS subject to substantive restrictions, independent sentencing reasons and written cautions, while leaving the internal weighting algorithm undisclosed and some input and report information available. The sufficiency and practical effectiveness of those protections can then be criticized explicitly. Each clause is supported by the cited paragraphs. This repairs the factual summary; it does not validate COMPAS, establish absence of bias, or resolve the policy disagreement. The incorrect 2018 date in the paper is not counted as a separate substantive issue.

Evidence: source_pages/source_p6.png and source_p7.png visually confirm the paper’s wording; sources/0034/conceptual_loomis_2016.pdf preserves the official opinion. The check is primary-source contradiction with a specified alternative reading, not a numerical counterexample or an empirical causal result.

Calibration dependency and judgment: Minor retained. The false warning-only/total-information-vacuum account strengthens one case illustration. Its correction still leaves the internal scoring mechanism undisclosed; available inputs permit some challenges without establishing sufficient model-level explanation. Section6, p.8, makes the proposed assessment conditional on technically supported notice and a fair opportunity to contest, and the separately checked K.W. notice/contestation evidence does not depend on Loomis. Thus the source correction alters the claimed extent of one case’s deficit without defeating those independent premises. This bounded factual role, rather than survival of a broad agenda, supports Minor. It does not validate the broadest incompatibility language, establish safeguard efficacy, or certify COMPAS safety or fairness.
# 4. Checks that did not establish additional defects
Checked material | Result and boundary

K.W. v. Armstrong, pp. 3-4 | The 2016 filed order [S3], pp. 11-15, supports the 733 usable records, major data attrition, underrepresentation, roughly 10-15% inadequate-budget estimate, and nearly 39% without a guardian/conservator. These are court-record figures, not independently recomputed population estimates.

Secrecy in the Idaho case | The 2016 order, pp. 21-24, specifically handles access to SIB-R assessment material and copyright/confidentiality concerns, including protective access. Earlier trade-secret resistance and disclosure of spreadsheet formulas are described by the plaintiffs’ lawyer in 2023 Senate testimony [S5], p. 3. The testimony supports the historical narrative but is not the earlier court order itself. Its absence from the 2016 order is not evidence that the event never happened.

Causal explanation and regression, pp. 2-5 | Coefficients require attention to units, coding, feature values and correlations; they are not automatically causal effects. No numerical coefficient ranking or causal estimator is supplied here that can be falsified. Treat the discussion as advice needing precise implementation, not an invalid derivation.

Neural networks, LLMs and trees, pp. 5-6 | The limited point that fluent explanations or saliency displays need not faithfully explain a decision is distinct from a universal claim that every explanation is meaningless. Deeper models do not universally improve out-of-sample accuracy. The paper supplies qualitative cautions rather than a testable scaling law or a proof of universal interpretability failure.

Broad incompatibility and alternatives, pp. 3-8 | Section 4 admits different levels of salvageability; p. 4 rejects banning statistical tools as such; Section 6 presents a conditional notice/hearing checklist. These qualifications favor a normative, deployment-specific reading over a literal theorem prohibiting every use of every AI model.

Usefulness versus determinative effect, p. 6 | An evidentiary item can corroborate other information or alter confidence without changing a particular final action. The rhetorical either/or should not be read as a formal proof. This clarification does not establish that COMPAS is useful or that judges avoid anchoring.

The case study supports serious process failures in the specified system. It does not furnish a controlled comparison of all modern AI systems with human decision-makers. No unmeasured efficacy or prevalence claim has been promoted to a verified empirical result.

Abstract-level checks of Adebayo et al. [S6] and Turpin et al. [S7] corroborate limitations of some saliency methods and possible unfaithfulness of generated explanations. They do not prove universal failure. Their experiments were not rerun and these checks do not establish the adequacy of any deployed legal procedure.
# 5. Dependence, versions and remaining evidence

As of 24 October 2026, a fresh download of the publisher-linked PDF is byte-for-byte identical to the frozen original (same 156,215 bytes and SHA-256); exact extracted text also matches. The citation gives ICML 13-19 July 2025, while the PMLR repository metadata records 6 October 2025 as its issue/post date. No separate arXiv version or labeled erratum was located in the bounded search. A related earlier CS&Law poster title was found, but no manuscript was retrieved and it is not treated as a verified prior version. OpenReview TEkyydR6il presented a browser-verification challenge, so its discussions and attachments were not inspected. Problem 1 remains in the current publisher bytes.

Problem 1 affects the legal description supporting the paper’s critique of the criminal-justice case. The broader research agenda remains available: improve accessible explanations, distinguish tool types, measure actual harms, permit meaningful challenge, and examine appropriate limits on deployment. The verified correction is a source-faithful rewrite only. Fresh empirical work would be needed to determine whether the Loomis safeguards change judges’ behavior, and deployment-specific legal and technical evidence would be needed to judge a particular system’s procedural adequacy.

No later case history was used to retroactively reject the paper’s 2025 account. A complete legal citator search, the entire K.W. docket, all legal and technical references, and contemporary model-specific interpretability capabilities were outside scope. No dedicated code or separate supplement was located in the bounded official-source search; absence of an artifact is not a defect for this position paper.
# 6. Conclusion and decision ledger
Decision item | Status and scope
Issue judgment | F1: Minor retained. Correct the extent of the Loomis deficit; the corrected record retains the specific undisclosed-mechanism premise, and K.W. evidence is independent.
Repair verification | Replacement checked against majority paragraphs 51-56 and 98-100. Safeguard efficacy and COMPAS safety are not established.
Author adoption | Not requested. No correction has been represented as accepted.
Other inspected claims | Idaho case: No Issue Found within checked scope. Technical and normative claims: scope clarifications, not additional demonstrated defects.
Remaining evidence | Earlier Idaho disclosure order and related poster manuscript not retrieved. Judicial-behavior experiments and deployment-specific analysis would be needed for stronger claims.
Scientific decision | Pending human adjudication and controller acceptance.
# 7. Consulted references

[S1] Rane, S. Position: AI’s growing due process problem. Proceedings of ICML 2025, PMLR 267:82062-82071. Frozen 10-page publisher PDF; accessed 24 October 2026. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/rane25b.html

report:
ELVIA Scientific Verification Report
I25-40139 / 0035
Paper: Position: AI Competitions Provide the Gold Standard for Empirical Rigor in GenAI Evaluation
Inspection outcome: Minor: one bounded inference defect; additional scope clarifications and evidence gaps
Reviewed version: Frozen publisher PDF, PMLR 267:82166-82178 (2025), 13 pages; SHA-256 recorded below
Batch token: `[internal identifier omitted]`
Review date: Review and severity calibration: 24 October 2026 (America/Chicago); machine logs use UTC
# 1. Identity, scope, and result

Reviewed D. Sculley and ten coauthors, ICML 2025 position paper [S1], OpenReview Rxd2TpV6Eg. Page numbers below are one-based PDF pages, matching the printed 1-13; they are not the continuous PMLR page range. The controller-supplied original has 878,066 bytes and SHA-256 `f532549cc870bd86cb1ac0f439e24fa493c3534cbc2aea3ea534f067ae7f8fa5`. Its identity and hash were checked before analysis and are checked again at delivery.

Read all Sections 1-8, both conceptual figures and captions, acknowledgments, and references. This is a position paper with no formal theorem, independent experimental results table, or appendix. Targeted primary-source checks cover ensemble reasoning, dynamic evaluation, prospective competition protocols, and the OpenVaccine example. A reviewer-created exact calculation was run; author code and competition experiments were not run.

One Minor issue is retained after claim-level calibration: negligible gains among submitted ensembles cannot bound gains from permitted, unsubmitted methods. The saved four-point counterexample remains decisive. The failed inference supplies Section8’s reassurance about deadline opportunity cost. Sections1.1,6 and7 instead ground the proposed evaluation standard in anti-cheating practices, contemporaneous comparisons and renewable tasks; those mechanisms do not require exhaustive model search. Other evidence gaps and their classifications are unchanged.
# 2. Definitions, assumptions, and review limits

A submitted-prediction ensemble is any rule whose test-time information is the vector of submitted predictions. The permitted hypothesis class may contain methods absent from that vector. Population accuracy is the objective in the diagnostic example. Its probabilities are known exactly, so the calculation has no sampling error or numerical tolerance. The example tests an implication in the argument; it is not a reconstruction of an actual Kaggle competition.

Three distinctions guide the other checks: data becoming public is different from its demonstrated incorporation into a particular model; newly curated annotations are different from newly discovered facts; and a benchmark pipeline that can be refreshed is different from a dated record of actual refreshes. Novelty restrictions define a target evaluation distribution and need not invalidate every use of IID sampling. Normative recommendations are assessed as proposals, without converting them into universal statistical theorems.

No complete audit of entrants’ training data, private leaderboard feedback, original competition submissions, or benchmark releases was possible. The reported median of 1,400 forum messages and individual historical leakage incidents were not independently recomputed. Bibliography reading and selected source verification are not an exhaustive reference audit. These limits are itemized in coverage.json.
# 3. Problem 1 — ensemble saturation is not an optimality certificate

Source and suspect step. Section 8, PDF p.9, left column, second paragraph, answers the objection that deadlines may exclude valuable work. It moves from the authors’ experience of little or no ensemble improvement to the conclusion that competitions extract nearly maximal signal within their constraints [S1]. The empirical observation may be accurate. The unsupported step is treating performance within the submitted prediction family as a bound on the larger permitted family.

Complete construction. Let X1 and X2 be independent Bernoulli(1/2) variables and let Y=X2. Both input coordinates are available to every competitor. Permit one-coordinate binary rules using either coordinate with the same simple model and input-access budget. The submitted rules are h1(X)=X1 and h2(X)=1-X1. The permitted but unsubmitted rule is g(X)=X2. There is no data leakage, access advantage, or more expensive model in g.
\[\begin{gathered}\Pr(X_1=a,X_2=b)=\tfrac14,\quad a,b\in\{0,1\},\qquad Y=X_2,\\ H_{\rm sub}(X)=(X_1,1-X_1),\qquad g(X)=X_2.\end{gathered}\]
Input (X1, X2) | Y | Submitted vector (h1,h2) | g

For either attainable prediction vector, the conditional label remains a fair bit. Thus every deterministic ensemble e(H_sub), including a combination learned from separate labeled data, has population accuracy 1/2. This is true even for an oracle selecting the best such map. Randomized rules are mixtures of deterministic rules and retain accuracy 1/2. Adding any number of submitted models whose joint predictions depend only on X1 leaves the same information limitation.

\[\begin{gathered}\sup_e \Pr(e(H_{\rm sub}(X))=Y)=\tfrac12=\max_i\Pr(h_i(X)=Y),\\ \Delta_{\rm ensemble}=0,\qquad \Pr(g(X)=Y)=1.\end{gathered}\] Finite verification. independent_check.py evaluates the four support points with exact rational arithmetic and enumerates all 16 binary lookup maps on the four possible binary prediction pairs. Only two pairs occur in this distribution, but checking all 16 maps covers every deterministic combination. Every map scores 1/2, both submitted models score 1/2, and g scores 1. All assertions passed under Python 3.13.5, with actual process exit code 0. The saved results are in verification/0035/independent_check_results.json.

Original-condition check. The paragraph supplies no formal model-class or search-coverage assumption. The example preserves its premises of available submissions, no improvement through aggregation, a common evaluation metric, and fixed competition constraints. It shows that those premises alone cannot imply nearly optimal attainable performance. It does not claim the actual competitions use this distribution, that entrants miss an obvious coordinate, or that their unsubmitted improvement is 50 percentage points.

Alternative readings and counterevidence. Diverse teams may provide useful practical evidence of broad search. That evidence still needs a connection to unexplored permitted methods. An ensemble that additionally accesses X2 and learns g has introduced a new information source and hypothesis; its success would not follow from earlier prediction-only saturation. The authors’ experiential observation remains unrefuted. Krogh and Vedelsby’s established ensemble analysis [S3] supplies related context about shared errors and prediction disagreement; its squared-loss identity is not used as a proof of this binary-accuracy example.

Calibrated dependency and judgment: Minor retained. Section8, p.9, uses the near-maximality inference to answer the objection that a deadline excludes valuable submissions. Because time bounds are part of the definition on p.1, this is a substantive failed rebuttal. However, Section1.1, p.2, locates the gold-standard rationale in anti-cheating practices and renewable tasks. Sections6.1-6.2, pp.7-8, describe contemporaneous comparisons and guarded/prospective test data; Section7, p.8, explicitly treats evaluations as point-in-time results. No method, metric, contamination-control mechanism or downstream recommendation is derived from exhaustive signal extraction. The demonstrated damage is consequently bounded to the unsupported reassurance about excluded approaches. This is a dependency-based Minor judgment, not one based on paper type, section placement, ease of repair or the general usefulness of competitions.

Alternative scope and supported repair. If competition constraints mean all permitted methods, the checked implication fails. If they mean only the submitted prediction family, saturation may describe that family but does not answer the deadline objection. Retain only the observed small gains among tested submissions and state that gains from unsubmitted permitted approaches are unbounded by that observation. A common cutoff supports contemporaneous comparison while exclusion of stronger approaches remains an unresolved tradeoff for renewed evaluations. This narrows the claim; it does not restore near-optimality or certify the categorical gold-standard recommendation. Actual missed gains and the authors’ historical ensemble record remain unmeasured here.
# 4. Other checked claims and evidence boundaries

IID, novelty, and exposure (Sections 2-5). Finite IID samples need not preserve every realized correlation. Within-dialogue dependence does not prevent independently sampling entire reset interactions. A fixed exclusion region around training examples changes the evaluation target, while mere absence of exact duplicates need not. These are scope clarifications; the paper acknowledges that task similarity needs definition. Its immediate invalidation of exposed tests is explicitly a conservative evaluation policy. This review does not interpret it as proof that every exposed item has entered model parameters.

Dynamic benchmarks (Section 5.2, p.6). LiveBench v2, Sections 2.7, 6 and A.6 [S4], confirms that newly collected questions are withheld for one month, with a private subset. The source specifies monthly rather than weekly collection; cadence wording alone is not treated as a substantive issue. The cited SWE-bench v3 [S5] describes 2,294 instances and a continually updatable collection pipeline. Evidence of actual frequent test-set updates for that specific benchmark version remains missing. Capability to refresh cannot substitute for release history; no later SWE-bench variant is silently substituted.

Prospective ground truth (Section 6.2, p.7). CAFA’s annotation-after-submission design is supported. The stronger statement that answers were unavailable to any human or model needs a publication-date check, because annotation dates need not equal experimental discovery dates. A later organizer preprint [S6], Sections 2.4 and 3.3, explicitly distinguishes these events. It is a June 2026 version, not peer reviewed, and analyzes an expanded evaluation using later annotations. Its subset percentages cannot be assigned to the original December 2023 competition. No original-cohort item/publication crosswalk was established here; no entrant contamination is demonstrated. Status: Needs Evidence for the universal knowledge claim, with the paper’s own ’reasonably leak-proof’ qualification retained.

Other prospective mechanisms (Section 6.2, pp.7-8). The AIMO2 organizer notice [S7] confirms a new 110-problem set at approximately National Olympiad difficulty. Official indexed WSDM content [S8a] supports a submission freeze followed by forecasting on newly acquired data. Konwinski’s official description likewise supports post-freeze GitHub issue collection [S8b]. The exact three-month interval was not independently reconstructed from a dated rules snapshot. No individual problem originality audit or guarantee of total contamination absence is claimed.

OpenVaccine (Section 8, p.9). The original article [S9], pp.1177 and 1179, supports a 25% private-test mean columnwise root mean squared error (MCRMSE) reduction against DegScore and blind validation on much longer 504-1,588-nucleotide molecules. Its three-week description is compatible with the position paper’s within-four-weeks wording. These concern RNA degradation prediction, not a measured vaccine shelf-life improvement or universal competition superiority. This positive example survives Problem 1.

Historical rankings and security. Primary abstracts [S10-S11] support the bounded observations of relative ranking stability and little detected leaderboard overfitting in the studied settings; absolute accuracy stability and universal immunity do not follow. Network isolation in Section 6.1 needs a full threat model covering returned scores and logs, but no actual competition exploit was established. The paper also acknowledges traditional leakage difficulty and requests ecological-validity studies. These are preserved qualifications, not additional proven defects.
# 5. Versions, released materials, and dependence

The current publisher PDF and a publisher-repository copy pinned to commit `a3e4112da70e3f0623daeb3eeea06e2b34ed5e2f` are byte-identical to the reviewed original. The publisher metadata records 6 October 2025, while ICML ran 13-19 July 2025. A repository commit message is not an erratum. No labeled correction was located in the bounded publisher/arXiv/author searches; OpenReview content could not be verified because of an access challenge.

arXiv 2505.00612 lists v1 (1 May 2025; 12 pages) and v2 (29 May 2025; 13 pages) [S2]. Both predate the conference. v2’s entire extracted text equals the frozen text after removal of its arXiv stamp and whitespace normalization; this is not a claim of binary or visual identity. The ensemble inference persists in the current publisher and v2 text. Earlier v1 differences were retained as history, not relabeled as current defects.

The official v2 source archive was captured and its meaningful nine-file tree preserved: manuscript TeX, bibliography, metadata, four style files, and two conceptual-figure PNGs. # Identity, reviewed version, and outcome

Reviewed source: publisher-linked ICML 2025 / PMLR volume 267 PDF, proceedings pp. 81410-81470, 61 PDF pages. All page numbers below mean the PDF’s printed pages 1-61, which match the physical PDF page index plus one. The publisher prints Manish Shetty; the task manifest’s longer name is treated as the same paper identity, not a scientific issue. [E1-E2]

The original PDF bytes match the controller acquisition receipt. The main text and expanded Appendices A-H were read. Two local evidentiary defects are supported: the displayed Verus postcondition already preserves the old logical queue elements, and the Astropy example reverses the explicitly requested operation. Both are Minor because they invalidate specific supporting examples without invalidating a central theorem, a reported experiment, or an inference that the broader taxonomy or research recommendations require. This judgment is based on their actual dependencies, not on their location in an appendix.

Scientific decisions remain pending. No human-review declaration is made. Author adoption has not been requested. This is a claim-focused verification report, not a certification of whole-paper correctness.
# Scope, definitions, and checked reasoning

Sections 1-6 (pp. 1-9) propose a task taxonomy, identify challenges in data, scale, interaction and measurement, and recommend data collection, training and inference-time research. Appendices A-H (pp. 27-61) expand the taxonomy, examples, recommendations, limitations and related work. The reference list (pp. 10-26) was used for source identification; its hundreds of entries were not individually audited.

Normative recommendations and predictions were distinguished from technical assertions. The paper does not present a new controlled experiment establishing that its proposed research directions work, and this review does not impose such a requirement. The checks target the accuracy of the concrete evidence offered for those recommendations.

For Problem 1, a queue’s logical contents are its Seq-valued view in the linked ring-buffer implementation. The old state is the state at function entry. The push operation appends one value to a finite sequence and retains every earlier index. Equality of whole sequences therefore implies equality of their old prefixes. The argument concerns active queue elements, not unchanged unused physical storage slots.

Static inspection covered the linked historical ring-buffer file and the Verus sequence specification, together with Astropy issue #14181 and PR #14182. No author code, proof checker, model, benchmark or training pipeline was executed. Primary-source snapshots and pinned repository paths are retained under sources/0036/.
# Problem 1: the displayed Verus specification already preserves prior elements

Source claim and location. Appendix D.2.3, p. 50, in the boxed Verus example, identifies failure to preserve the original ring-buffer elements as an omitted postcondition. The same box displays the branch-sensitive whole-sequence relation below. The source page was visually inspected. [E1, E5-E6]

Complete analytic check. Let q be the old logical sequence, q’ the post-state sequence, and n the length of q. If ret is true, the displayed clause gives q’ = q.push(val). By the indexed definition of sequence append, q’[i] = q[i] for every integer i with 0 <= i < n; q’ has length n+1 and its last element is val. If ret is false, the clause gives q’ = q, so every previous element is again retained. These are the only two Boolean branches. Thus the exact omission alleged in the prose is already excluded by the displayed postcondition.

\[\forall\,i\in\mathbb{Z},\quad 0\le i<|q|\ \Longrightarrow\ q'_i=q_i.\] Assumptions and independent source check. In the linked prepublication implementation, View for RingBuffer<T> has V = Seq<T>; its view enumerates the stored elements from head to tail modulo capacity. The inspected implementation also writes preservation as an explicit indexed equality in its enqueue contract. The two formulations agree on this property. This is a semantic argument about the printed contract, not a claim that the printed implementation was mechanically verified, or that all necessary preconditions are printed in the box.

Alternative readings and counterevidence. A different, unfaithful view abstraction could make a postcondition irrelevant to physical contents; the linked view explicitly maps to the active stored elements, so that escape does not explain this example. A client using only a weaker trait-level contract may know less, but that is different from the concrete contract shown in the paper. The box could still omit other requirements, including a particular capacity policy; this review does not assert complete specification adequacy. The precise preservation accusation fails.

Impact and repair status. The example does not demonstrate the stated autoformalization failure. This is a local defect in evidence supporting D.2.3’s recommendation to refine specifications interactively. No downstream theorem or quantitative result depends on the alleged omission, and the separate argument that formal specifications can fail to capture intent is not contradicted. Remove or replace this example, or explicitly discuss a genuinely missing property. The preservation implication is analytically verified; a replacement example and its model provenance are not verified. Supported judgment: Minor.
# Problem 2: the Astropy example reverses the issue’s explicit request

Source claim and location. Appendix C.3, p. 38, in the serializer-deserializer box, describes astropy #14181 as requesting a new reStructuredText input format, treats writing as an implicit requirement, and reports that models implemented only reading. The source page was visually inspected. [E1, E3-E4]

Complete source comparison. The primary issue is titled ’Please support header rows in RestructuredText output’. Its reproducer first successfully calls tbl.write with format=’ascii.rst’, then requests header_rows for that same output format. The failure is an unexpected header_rows argument. Output is therefore explicit, and basic support for the format already exists. This does not match either the claimed input direction or the claimed introduction of a new format.

PR #14182 strengthens and limits the conclusion. Its patch adds configurable header rows and adjusts both read and write paths, with a round-trip test. Consequently the example may have a repairable directional reversal: reading may be the implicit companion to an explicitly requested writing feature. That possibility is counterevidence to any claim that the broad serializer-deserializer principle itself fails.

Unresolved model provenance. The issue and human-authored PR establish what was requested and repaired. They do not identify the exact model, prompt, patch or evaluation run underlying the paper’s behavioral allegation. This review does not infer whether a published model implemented only read, only write, or both. A mistaken issue identifier or reversed narration could explain the discrepancy, but neither is demonstrated.

Impact and precise supported correction. Correct the description to an explicit request for header-row support in an existing reStructuredText output writer. That textual correction is supported by the primary issue. It does not by itself restore the alleged model-failure example; that requires the actual evaluation patch and a faithful comparison with the request. The existing narration cannot support an inference about missing implicit writing behavior. This bounded evidentiary defect is Minor; the unverified model behavior remains Needs Evidence and does not raise the paper’s supported severity.
# Other checks, counterevidence, and dependency assessment

The appendix’s p. 33 square-invariant example depends on integer semantics: mathematical integers, checked/no-overflow executions and fixed-width wraparound integers differ. Because the paper does not identify the language or integer model, this was retained as a scope clarification rather than promoted into a demonstrated counterexample satisfying its operative assumptions.

The p. 35 CompCert description must be understood within the verified compiler transformations and trusted components. No central claim was rejected solely for compressed overview wording. The p. 4 Qwen language-accuracy comparison was investigated against the cited technical report, but the exact size/version and D-language comparison were not independently resolved; it remains an evidence limitation, not a demonstrated numerical error. The p. 9 SWE-bench progress comparison was not reconstructed to a common subset and evaluation configuration.

The dependency of the confirmed defects is specific: the p. 50 box supports the discussion of incomplete formalizations in D.2.3; the p. 38 box supports the discussion of implicit requirements in C.3. Neither supports a new claimed theorem or a measured effect size, and neither is the only premise offered for the paper’s task taxonomy or proposed research directions. The findings therefore concern two examples. Other examples and citations have only the coverage described in the ledger; their survival is not a proof that all of them are correct.

Version check. The publisher-linked PDF is the review target. A related arXiv record, 2503.22625v1, dated 28 March 2025, has a different title, a 75-page scope and additional authors; it was not silently substituted for this 61-page conference version. Publisher and related-version metadata were checked. OpenReview’s direct web page presented a browser-verification wall, so its full discussion and revision history were not inspected. No claim of an exhaustive erratum search or verified later repair is made.

report: ELVIA Scientific Verification / ICML 2025 / I25-40142
Position: LLMs Need a Bayesian Meta-Reasoning Framework for More Robust and Generalizable Reasoning
Supported judgment: Major. Scientific decision: pending.
Review date: 2026-10-24. Batch token: `[internal identifier omitted]`.
# Identity, reviewed version, and concise outcome

Reviewed: Hanqi Yan, Linhai Zhang, Jiazheng Li, Zhenyi Shen and Yulan He; ICML 2025, PMLR 267:82360-82383; publisher-linked 24-page PDF. References to pages mean printed PDF pages, identical to 1-based physical pages. The exact original bytes match the controller acquisition receipt. [E1-E2]

Code:
SHA-256: d53050e10a1dae438eea6ed076257fe5e57464cbde90cef66ff3983531c632fc

Supported judgment: Major for an invalid core meta-level posterior update in Section 3.1. The left side conditions on the reasoning strategy F, while the right side marginalizes F out. A fully positive finite hierarchical model gives a correct posterior of 0.90 where the printed expression gives 0.74 after normalization. This is a demonstrated error in the mathematical formulation central to the proposed Bayesian framework, not an objection that a position paper lacks experiments.

The cognitive architecture, literature taxonomy and proposed research directions are not thereby disproved. Their survival is separate from the severity of the false central update. Scientific decisions and human review remain pending; author adoption has not been requested.
# Scope, model definitions, and assumptions

The review covered Sections 1-7 (pp. 1-9), Figures 1-5, Table 1 and the Bayesian expressions, plus the full literature appendix (pp. 21-24). References (pp. 10-20) were used selectively. Static inspection of the linked public repository found resource lists and diagrams, not an executable implementation of the proposed update. No author code, LLM, reward model or benchmark was run.

Write theta = (theta_I, theta_E) for internal and external knowledge variables, F for a reasoning strategy, A for a reasoning trajectory and O for observed feedback. Section 3.1 gives strategy generation p(F|theta), trajectory generation p(A|F), and feedback p(O|A). We hold any external goal/context fixed. The counterexample uses independent knowledge priors, exactly as the product prior on the printed right side allows.

Figure 2 also permits direct knowledge-to-observation effects. The witness selects the admissible submodel in which these effects vanish. No faithfulness or nonzero-effect assumption is stated. Every probability of every binary joint assignment remains positive. The paper does not restrict latent support to continuous densities; for a finite strategy set the integral is its standard sum analogue. If F itself represents a skill distribution, its two values can label two distinct such distributions.
# Problem 1: a conditional posterior is replaced by a marginal posterior

Source claim and exact location. At the bottom of p. 3, Section 3.1, under ’Updating knowledge priors at the meta-level’, the paper labels the following quantity as the posterior over knowledge priors. The original rendered page was visually checked. [E1]

\[p(\theta_I,\theta_E\mid O,F)\ \propto\ \left[\int p(O\mid f)\,p(f\mid\theta_I,\theta_E)\,df\right]p(\theta_I)p(\theta_E).\] Suspect step. Integrating over f removes the realized strategy from the evidence. Under the stated Markov simplification, the right side is an unnormalized p(theta|O), not p(theta|O,F). Its dependence on theta cannot generally be repaired by a scalar normalizing constant. This is a target-distribution mismatch.

Dependency. This is the second level of the paper’s central two-level Bayesian learning scheme, immediately following Eq. (2) and Table 1. Section 3.2 uses meta-reflection to update knowledge and strategies, and Section 4.4 describes refining F and then optimizing the meta-parameters. Consequently the incorrect expression affects the proposed mechanism for consolidating knowledge across tasks. It is not a peripheral numerical example or a bibliography defect.
# Problem 1 continued: a complete positive-probability counterexample

All five variables I=theta_I, E=theta_E, F, A and O are binary. I and E are independent Bernoulli(1/2). The remaining conditional tables are below; probabilities of value zero are the complements. E is a genuine random variable but its effect on F is set to zero.
Conditional probability | Parent value 0 | Parent value 1
P(O=1 | A), parent A | 1/8 | 7/8

\[p(i,e,f,a,o)=p(i)p(e)p(f\mid i,e)p(a\mid f)p(o\mid a).\] Assumption check. Each conditional table sums to one. Exact enumeration gives total joint mass 1, all 32 joint assignments strictly positive, and minimum mass 1/3200. No zero-likelihood event, undefined conditioning, dependent prior, invalid strategy value or negative weight is used. The event O=1,F=1 has probability 2/5. The independent reviewer script uses Python Fraction arithmetic and does not import or execute author code. [E4]

\[\Pr(O=1\mid F=0)=\frac9{10}\frac18+\frac1{10}\frac78=\frac15,\qquad \Pr(O=1\mid F=1)=\frac45.\] Correct result when F=1 and O=1 are given. Conditional independence makes the O likelihood common to both values of I. The posterior probability of I=1 is therefore 9/10. Equivalently, its numerator is (1/2)(9/10)(4/5)=9/25 and the event probability is 2/5.

\[\Pr(I=1\mid O=1,F=1)=\frac{9/25}{2/5}=\frac9{10}=0.90.\] Printed-right-side result. Marginalizing F yields likelihood 13/50 for I=0 and 37/50 for I=1. Multiplying each by its 1/2 prior and normalizing gives 37/50=0.74 for I=1. The exact joint meta-parameter probability is also different: the correct P(I=1,E=1|O=1,F=1)=9/20=0.45, whereas the printed normalized right side gives 37/100=0.37.

\[\frac{(1/2)(37/50)}{(1/2)(13/50+37/50)}=\frac{37}{50}\ne\frac9{10}.\] The disagreement survives normalization: the correct odds for I=1 versus I=0 are 9, while the printed odds are 37/13. When the conditioned strategy is changed to F=0, the correct posterior is 0.10, but the integrated expression still gives 0.74. Thus the formula loses information that its left side explicitly conditions on. Analytic Bayes calculations and exact finite enumeration agree.
# Alternative interpretations, scoped corrections, and impact

Strongest alternative reading. The left side may be mislabeled and the authors may intend the marginal posterior p(theta|O). Under the simplifying conditional-independence assumptions, that reading makes the integral mathematically appropriate. It changes the inferential target and must be stated explicitly. Table 1 samples F from a strategy prior and Eq. (2) updates its posterior, so neither passage makes the conditioned F on the left side a harmless dummy integration variable.

If F is instead a controlled intervention, or a distribution over strategies rather than an observed latent value, the update must specify that interpretation and the corresponding probability measure. Those are reasonable design choices, but the paper does not supply such a reinterpretation of the displayed conditional posterior. It is not valid to silently use them to equate two demonstrably different distributions.

Two precise mathematical repairs are available; they represent different algorithms. For a strategy fixed as evidence, retain F=f and remove the integral. For an uncertain strategy marginalized out, remove F from the left-side conditioning. The general likelihood may depend on theta; retain that dependence when the graph permits it.

\[p(\theta\mid O,F=f)\propto p(O\mid f,\theta)\,p(f\mid\theta)\,p(\theta).\] \[p(\theta\mid O)\propto p(\theta)\int p(O\mid f,\theta)\,p(f\mid\theta)\,df.\] Both identities are analytically supported and distinguish the counterexample’s 0.90 and 0.74 results. They do not establish which learning rule the authors intend, how repeated evidence should be managed, how rewards become calibrated likelihoods, or that an eventual implementation improves LLM performance. Those parts of a repaired framework are unverified.

Supported severity: Major. The invalid equality defines the core meta-level update, a central technical contribution, and the counterexample demonstrates a materially different inferred knowledge posterior. Neither the ease of changing notation nor the survival of the broad meta-reasoning proposal reduces that demonstrated core derivation error to Minor. No empirical-score deterioration or refutation of the entire research agenda is needed for this judgment.
# Other inspected claims, versions, and conclusion

The reward-to-likelihood proportionality in Table 1 is underspecified as a normalized generative model, but a Gibbs or generalized-Bayes interpretation is plausible. It is recorded as a required implementation clarification, not a separate demonstrated failure. Section 4.4’s inverse-planning and reward-proxy suggestions are prospective proposals. Sections 5-7 offer research directions rather than a new controlled evaluation; their lack of experimental validation is not counted as an error.

The full appendix summarizes existing methods. Selective checks of the Qwen2.5 training summary and the contextual R1-Zero discussion supplied counterevidence against treating condensed descriptions as standalone defects. No additional substantive error is supported by those checks. The review does not verify every cited performance statement.

Version/source scope. The publisher PDF is the target. The linked resources repository is pinned at commit `2569e3ddf8ab063cfab28be819c998c4913a2431` (29 July 2025), tree `8c4b10a86bfcaaa6f3eb4dbe0c63d355d21d4eef`; its 10 files consist of three Markdown files and seven diagrams.
